title: Mining and Mercury: How Sure Are You?

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *puede* (maybe), *debe de* (probably) and *tiene que* (almost sure) + infinitive from B2 Unit 26, and *haber* + participle for the past. A text about illegal gold mining has to say what is known and what is only likely. Here the guesses work on mercury in the rivers.

sections.title: From less sure to more sure
rows: El mercurio puede llegar a los peces del río.
Si los peces tienen mercurio, debe de haber minas cerca.
*debe de*: a good guess from a sign
Si los análisis muestran mercurio y no hay fábricas cerca, tiene que venir de la minería.
*tiene que*: almost sure, no other explanation
Los peces pueden haber recibido el mercurio de las aguas río arriba.
*puede haber* + participle: a possible cause in the past

items.spanish: Un pez que come otros peces puede tener más mercurio.
items.english: A fish that eats other fish may have more mercury.

items.spanish: Debe de haber mucho mercurio en ese tramo del río.
items.english: There must be a lot of mercury in that stretch of the river.

items.spanish: Tiene que ser mercurio: el análisis lo muestra.
items.english: It has to be mercury: the analysis shows it.

sections.content: *Tiene que ser* is a guess because the verb is *ser* or *estar*. *Tiene que salir* is a need, not a guess. For a guess about the past add *haber* + participle (*debe de haber llegado*). Say who gives the information when you report a figure or a diagnosis.
